It will estimate net community production and carbon-export rates and compare biological and physical controls on future Southern Ocean oxygen and carbon budgets. The project began in August 2026 and is scientific observation and modelling rather than engineered removal or credit certification.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 August 2026 to 31 July 2028.

document_title: SIPODET — Simultaneous Chemical Imaging of Coastal Seagrass Microenvironments
notes: The Horizon 2020 SIPODET project proposed simultaneous imaging of several chemicals in Zostera marina and Zostera noltei microenvironments using planar optodes and diffusive-equilibrium thin films. The technology was intended to reveal chemical gradients and stress responses in seagrass ecosystems that provide carbon-sequestration and coastal-protection services. CORDIS contains inconsistent termination and planned-date metadata; the record is therefore treated as ended research and not as completed technology validation or verified blue-carbon removal.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: CORDIS lists planned dates of 1 June 2020 to 31 May 2022 but also records termination on 21 June 2019; this apparent metadata inconsistency is preserved rather than resolved by inference.

document_title: CRYOMICS — Cryosphere-Ocean Effects on Southern Ocean Microbial Communities
notes: The Marie Skłodowska-Curie CRYOMICS project investigates how freshwater, nutrients, trace metals and carbon released by the melting cryosphere affect phytoplankton, sea-ice algae and microbial communities in the eastern Weddell Gyre. Sampling, biogeochemical analysis and metagenomics are used to assess implications for primary production and biological carbon export. The project was active through August 2026 and did not constitute deliberate fertilization, verified removal or carbon-credit issuance.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 September 2024 to 31 August 2026.

document_title: CEFMED — Climate Effects on Deep-Sea Ecosystem Functioning in the Mediterranean Sea
notes: The FP7 CEFMED project investigated how changes in upper-ocean temperature, stratification, primary production and carbon export affect deep-sea ecosystem functioning in the Mediterranean. It examined food availability, benthic communities and climate-driven shifts in organic-matter supply to the seabed. The project was completed as ecosystem and carbon-cycle research and did not establish a seabed carbon-removal activity, restoration programme or crediting method.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 19 September 2013 to 18 September 2015.

document_title: PHYTOCHANGE — Phytoplankton Responses to Global Change
notes: The European Research Council funded PHYTOCHANGE to assess phytoplankton responses to warming, acidification and other global-change pressures. The project addressed diatom-driven organic-carbon export, coccolithophore control of ocean alkalinity through calcification and nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria as regulators of reactive nitrogen and productivity. It was completed as fundamental and experimental research and did not authorize ocean fertilization, alkalinity enhancement or carbon-credit issuance.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 June 2008 to 31 May 2013.

document_title: ABYSS — Assessment of Bacterial Life and Matter Cycling in Deep-Sea Surface Sediments
notes: The European Research Council funded ABYSS to investigate bacterial communities, organic-matter degradation and element cycling in deep-sea surface sediments. The project combined in-situ flux studies, isotope-labelled substrates, molecular tools and long-term Arctic observations to determine how benthic bacteria remineralise sinking organic matter and how the fraction escaping degradation contributes to geological carbon storage. It was completed as fundamental research and did not establish an engineered sequestration project, carbon-credit methodology or deployment authorization.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 June 2012 to 31 May 2018; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: MICROENERGY — Microbial Life under Extreme Energy Limitation
notes: The European Research Council funded MICROENERGY to examine microbial communities buried in marine sediments and living near the energetic limit for cellular activity. The project focused on methanogenesis, turnover of living and dead microbial biomass, metabolic energy fluxes and the role of subsurface carbon mineralisation in seabed methane cycling. It was completed as fundamental deep-biosphere research and did not establish microbial carbon-removal engineering, a deployment programme or verified carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 April 2012 to 31 March 2017; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: DEEP CARBON FLUX — Energy and Carbon Food Webs of the Deep Sub-Seafloor Biosphere
notes: The FP7 project investigated energetic and kinetic controls on organic-matter mineralisation in deeply buried marine sediments. It developed sensitive analytical methods for small organic acids and linked substrate turnover with sulfate reduction, methanogenesis and microbial energy fluxes across coastal, North Pacific and Baltic sediment systems. The project was completed as research and did not create a sub-seafloor carbon-removal technology, storage authorization or carbon-credit methodology.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 October 2013 to 4 November 2015; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: HADES — Benthic Diagenesis and Microbiology of Hadal Trenches
notes: The European Research Council funded HADES to quantify benthic metabolism and microbial processes in some of the deepest ocean trenches. The project developed autonomous in-situ instrumentation and compared trenches from contrasting ocean settings to determine how organic material is deposited, mineralised and processed by microbial and viral communities. It was completed as deep-sea carbon-cycle research and did not establish a biomass-burial engineering project, deployment authorization or crediting method.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 January 2016 to 31 December 2021; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: HYADES — Hydrostatic Pressure and Prokaryotic Activity in the Deep Sea
notes: The Horizon 2020 project examined how hydrostatic pressure affects prokaryotic activity and organic-matter degradation in the deep ocean. It addressed a mismatch between measured deep-sea microbial carbon demand and the supply of sinking organic carbon, using pressure-controlled experiments and microbial and biogeochemical analyses. The project was completed as research and did not create a microbial sequestration technology, official MRV standard or verified removal claim.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 15 April 2016 to 14 April 2018; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: OCTANT — Chronology of Deep-Ocean Circulation Changes during Abrupt Climate Transitions
notes: The Horizon 2020 project used coupled Earth-system and ice-sheet modelling to investigate the chronology, transport pathways and ventilation changes of the deep ocean during abrupt climate transitions. Because deep-ocean circulation controls the storage and release of large quantities of carbon, the research supported more reliable interpretation of sediment records and future climate projections. It did not constitute engineered ocean storage, a deployment activity or a carbon-credit methodology.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 19 March 2016 to 18 March 2018; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: CACH — Equatorial Atlantic Chemistry, Circulation and Deep-Water Habitat Reconstruction
notes: The European Research Council funded CACH to reconstruct abrupt changes in equatorial Atlantic chemistry, circulation and deep-water habitats using deep-sea coral records, geochemical analyses, field expeditions and modelling. The project examined how ocean circulation stores and releases heat and carbon during major climate transitions. It was completed as palaeoceanographic and ecosystem research and did not establish engineered carbon storage, a permit or a crediting mechanism.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 October 2011 to 30 September 2017; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: BIODEM — Biogeochemical and Physical Drivers of Deep European Margin Ecosystems
notes: The FP6 BIODEM project investigated sediment transport, organic-matter inputs, seabed composition, currents and biological communities in Mediterranean canyons and cold-water coral systems. Submarine canyons were treated as major pathways for organic-carbon transport and burial from continental margins to the deep sea. The project supported ecosystem understanding and marine-management decisions and did not establish a carbon-removal intervention, restoration credit or deployment authorization.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 April 2006 to 31 March 2008; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: SOCGDGT — Lipid Proxy for Marine Sediment Oxygen Consumption
notes: The Marie Skłodowska-Curie project develops a lipid-based proxy for sediment oxygen consumption using branched glycerol dialkyl glycerol tetraethers produced by benthic marine bacteria. The work links biomarker lipids, oxygen microprofiles, microbial communities and geochemistry to quantify organic-matter degradation and preservation in modern and palaeo marine sediments. The project was active in August 2026 and had not established an official monitoring standard, verified carbon storage or a crediting method.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 September 2024 to 31 August 2026; the project remained active as of 6 August 2026.

document_title: SUBSTRATE USE — Carbon-Cycling Microbes in Anoxic Marine Sediments
notes: The FP7 project investigated how sulfate reducers, methanogens and acetogens consume low-molecular-weight carbon compounds in anoxic marine sediments from Denmark, Mexico and the Bering Sea. Stable-isotope probing linked substrate consumption to microbial identity and clarified how organic matter is remineralised or preserved in the seafloor, one of Earth's largest organic-carbon sinks. The completed project did not create a microbial removal technology, storage permit or carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 January 2011 to 31 December 2012; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: CARBON TRANSFER — Trophic Carbon Transfer Efficiency under Carbon Dioxide Stress
notes: The FP6 project tested how increased dissolved carbon dioxide and lower seawater pH alter phytoplankton biochemical composition, carbohydrate release, zooplankton feeding, growth and reproduction. The work assessed whether ocean acidification could change coastal food-web efficiency and the transfer of photosynthetically fixed carbon through marine ecosystems. It was completed as experimental research and did not constitute ocean alkalinity enhancement, engineered removal or a carbon-credit programme.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 January 2007 to 31 December 2008; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: NAUTILOS — Low-Cost Underwater Technologies for Ocean Observation
notes: The Horizon 2020 NAUTILOS project developed, integrated and demonstrated cost-effective sensors and samplers for essential ocean variables, including inorganic carbon, nutrients, oxygen, phytoplankton and zooplankton. The technologies were deployed from coastal settings to the deep sea and were designed to expand the spatial and temporal coverage of European ocean observations and policy applications. The project strengthened monitoring infrastructure but did not establish a statutory marine CDR MRV standard, authorize deployment or verify carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 October 2020 to 30 June 2025; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: BARIUM — Barium Cycling in Antarctic Waters and Ocean Carbon Storage
notes: The FP7 BARIUM project investigated organic and inorganic carbon storage around the West Antarctic Peninsula using modern and palaeoceanographic barium cycling and isotope measurements. The work linked biological productivity, Southern Ocean circulation, nutrient distribution and carbon uptake across present and past climate conditions. It was completed as proxy and carbon-cycle research and did not establish an engineered sequestration activity, official accounting method or carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 October 2012 to 30 September 2016; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: ECoCT — Carbon Transformation during Serpentinization in the Oceanic Lithosphere
notes: The Marie Skłodowska-Curie project recreates seawater-rock interactions beneath the ocean floor to investigate carbon transformation, migration and reactivity during serpentinization. Open-system experiments, chemical analysis, microstructural characterisation and three-dimensional imaging are intended to clarify how abiotic and biological processes influence carbon storage in oceanic rocks and inform future storage technologies. The project was active in August 2026 and did not authorize injection, certify mineralised carbon or establish a commercial storage pathway.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 September 2024 to 31 August 2026; the project remained active as of 6 August 2026.

document_title: MANGROVE — Ecosystem, Community and Conflict Management in Southeast Asian Mangroves
notes: The FP6 project assessed mangrove ecosystem functions, adjacent coastal areas, household livelihoods, institutions, legislation, stakeholder values and conflicts at sites in Indonesia, Thailand and Vietnam. It developed participatory monitoring methods and implemented stakeholder action plans intended to reconcile conservation and resource-use demands. The project did not quantify blue-carbon removal, establish a carbon-credit methodology or report verified sequestration; it is included as foundational governance and management research for a major coastal blue-carbon ecosystem.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 August 2005 to 30 June 2010; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: Environmental Change Effects on European Salt Marsh Structure, Functioning and Coastal Exchange
notes: The European research project examined how environmental change alters the structure and functioning of salt marshes and their exchanges with adjacent coastal waters. It assessed organic and inorganic matter, sediment, nutrient and particulate-organic-matter transfers and sought management criteria for maintaining salt-marsh functions. The project provided foundational evidence for a major coastal blue-carbon habitat, but it did not implement restoration, quantify additional carbon removal or establish a crediting methodology.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 January 1993 to 30 June 1995; the project is closed.

document_title: Influence of Rising Sea Level on Ecosystem Dynamics of Salt Marshes
notes: The project investigated whether European salt marshes can persist under accelerated sea-level rise by analysing inundation, sediment accretion, surface elevation and interactions between physical and biological processes. The work supported understanding of salt-marsh resilience and future restoration requirements. It was a scientific research project and did not itself restore marshes, certify carbon sequestration or create blue-carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 February 1998 to 31 January 2001; the project is closed.

document_title: STORM — Stemming the Rising Tide: The Protective Role of Saltmarshes
notes: The Marie Skłodowska-Curie project examined the capacity of salt marshes to keep pace with sea-level rise and reduce wave energy. It linked sediment accretion, below-ground root growth, organic-matter accumulation and vegetation structure with coastal-protection performance. The completed research strengthened the evidence base for salt-marsh conservation and restoration, but it did not quantify additional carbon removal, approve a restoration project or issue credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2016; the project is closed.

document_title: ForCry — Analysing Frozen Foraminifera by Cryostage LA-ICPMS
notes: The European Research Council project develops cryogenic laser-ablation methods and boron-isotope measurements in foraminifera to improve reconstructions of seawater pH, atmospheric carbon dioxide and ocean carbon fluxes during the Neogene. The work strengthens carbonate-system proxies and long-term understanding of ocean carbon-cycle sensitivity. It is active research and does not constitute engineered mineralisation, an official carbon-accounting method or verified carbon removal.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 June 2022 to 31 May 2027.

document_title: CD-PALEO — Cadmium Isotope Measurements for Marine Sediments and Palaeoceanography
notes: The FP6 project developed cadmium-isotope measurements using a double-spike MC-ICP-MS approach and applied them to marine sediments and palaeoceanography. Cadmium distributions and isotopes provide information on nutrient utilisation, biological productivity, circulation and carbon-cycle changes. The project was completed as analytical and proxy research and did not establish a statutory monitoring requirement, engineered sequestration activity or carbon-credit methodology.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 December 2004 to 30 November 2006; the project is closed.

document_title: VARIO — Natural pH Variability and Ecosystem Response to Ocean Acidification
notes: The Horizon 2020 project was designed to test how natural pH variability affects the response of rhodolith-bed organisms and ecosystems to ocean acidification in Scotland and Greenland. The proposed work included field observations and experiments on calcification, physiology and ecosystem sensitivity. CORDIS records termination before the planned start date, so the record is treated as ended and does not imply completed experiments, an alkalinity intervention or verified carbon removal.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: CORDIS lists planned dates of 1 August 2019 to 31 July 2021 and records termination on 23 May 2019; the metadata inconsistency is preserved without inference.

document_title: DEstiNi — Dynamic Estuarine and Marine Cycling of Nickel
notes: The Horizon 2020 project investigated nickel cycling and isotope behaviour across estuarine, coastal and marine systems. It linked micronutrient supply, biological uptake, particle transport and sediment preservation with primary production and export carbon, including information from salt-marsh sediment cores. The completed project improved marine-carbon proxy interpretation but did not establish an official accounting method, restoration programme or carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 September 2019 to 22 August 2023; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: DINOPRO — Dinoflagellates as Proxies for Climate and Carbon Cycling
notes: The European Research Council project developed dinoflagellate-based signals for reconstructing climate, carbon cycling, surface-ocean carbon dioxide and acidification during past and present rapid carbon-cycle transitions. Culture experiments, carbon-isotope analysis and geological records were used to evaluate proxy performance. The project was completed as palaeoclimate research and did not establish engineered carbon removal, a regulatory accounting standard or carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 September 2010 to 31 August 2016; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: IsoMargin — Isotopes of Micronutrients to Trace Margin Sediment Fluxes
notes: The Horizon Europe project used copper, nickel and zinc isotopes to trace micronutrient fluxes from continental-margin sediments to the ocean. These micronutrients influence phytoplankton growth and the biological carbon pump, while isotope measurements help distinguish sedimentary sources and transformations. The project was completed as proxy and process research and did not establish a mandatory MRV method, engineered removal activity or carbon-credit system.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 October 2022 to 30 September 2024; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: MixOCarb — The Role of Mixotrophs in the Oceanic Carbon Cycle
notes: The FP7 project investigated organisms that combine photosynthesis and consumption of organic matter and assessed how mixotrophy changes production, respiration and carbon transfer in marine food webs. The research used molecular, physiological and single-cell methods to quantify diversity and activity and improve representation of mixotrophs in ocean-carbon models. It was completed as fundamental research and did not establish microbial carbon-removal engineering or verified removal credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 April 2015 to 31 March 2018; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: WET HORIZONS — Fast-Tracking Wetland Restoration across Europe
notes: The Horizon Europe project upgrades knowledge and practical tools for restoring European wetlands, including coastal wetlands, while assessing carbon sequestration, greenhouse-gas emissions, biodiversity and ecosystem services. It develops restoration guidance, spatial information, decision-support tools and policy dialogue intended to accelerate implementation. The project was active as of 6 August 2026 and does not by itself certify carbon credits or prove permanent project-level removal.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 September 2022 to 31 August 2026; the project remained active as of 6 August 2026.

document_title: RESTORE4Cs — Restoring Wetlands for Carbon Pathways and Climate Benefits
notes: The Horizon Europe project assessed European coastal-wetland restoration through pilot sites, harmonised measurements, remote sensing, modelling and machine learning. It developed standardised methods and decision-support tools for evaluating carbon storage, greenhouse-gas abatement, biodiversity, ecosystem services and restoration priorities. The project closed in 2025. Its outputs support planning and accounting, but the funding record does not itself issue carbon credits or certify permanent additional removal.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2025; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: ECOTIP — Arctic Biodiversity Change and Ecosystem Tipping Cascades
notes: The Horizon 2020 ECOTIP project assessed how climate-driven tipping cascades affect Arctic marine biodiversity, ecosystem functioning, carbon sequestration and dependent human systems. It integrated observations, experiments, ecological models, monitoring indicators and engagement with Indigenous and local communities. The completed project supported international governance and adaptation planning but did not establish an engineered carbon-removal activity, project-level MRV method or crediting programme.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 June 2020 to 31 May 2024; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

subnational_area: Southern Patagonia and West Antarctic Peninsula
document_title: CoastCarb — Coastal Ecosystem Carbon Balance in Times of Rapid Glacier Melt
notes: The Horizon 2020 CoastCarb network examined carbon budgets and flows in fjord and estuarine ecosystems of Southern Patagonia and the West Antarctic Peninsula. It integrated benthic and pelagic food webs, microbial processes, ecosystem modelling, open data and stakeholder analysis to understand climate-mitigation services under rapid glacier melt and human pressure. The project closed in 2025 and did not establish engineered removal, a crediting method or verified additional sequestration.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 January 2020 to 31 July 2025; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: FROM — Functional Redundancy of the Global Ocean Microbiome
notes: The Marie Skłodowska-Curie project evaluated functional redundancy in the global ocean microbiome by integrating taxonomic, genomic, environmental and dispersal information. It assessed how microbial communities maintain biogeochemical functions despite changes in species composition and environmental conditions. The project was completed as foundational marine-microbiome research. It did not directly quantify carbon sequestration, test a negative-emissions intervention or establish a carbon-credit methodology.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 April 2022 to 31 March 2024; CORDIS lists the project as closed.
